q: Which architect got his first major commission at about 50?
n: Louis Kahn got his first major commission, the Yale University Art Gallery (1951–53), at about age 50. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Louis Kahn.

q: What is the tallest building in the world?
n: The Burj Khalifa in Dubai (828 m) is the tallest building in the world. Source: CTBUH Skyscraper Center.

q: Who designed the Yale University Art Gallery?
n: The Yale University Art Gallery (1953) was designed by Louis Kahn. Source: Yale University Art Gallery history.

q: Which complex has a 70th-floor observation deck that opened in 1933, about 850 ft above the street?
n: Rockefeller Center's Top of the Rock observation deck on the 70th floor of 30 Rockefeller Plaza opened in 1933, about 850 ft above the street. Source: Rockefeller Center official site.

q: Which hotel has an elegant sail-like form?
n: The Burj Al Arab in Dubai (1999) has a sail-like form imitating a dhow's sail. Source: Jumeirah Burj Al Arab official site.

q: Which museum has a spiral ramp in a conical form?
n: Frank Lloyd Wright's Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum in New York (1959) has a continuous spiral ramp in an inverted conical form. Source: Guggenheim official site; UNESCO (20th-century Architecture of Frank Lloyd Wright).

q: Which neo-futurist residential tower is made of nine stacked cubes that twist 90° from base to top?
n: Turning Torso in Malmö, by Santiago Calatrava (2005), stacks nine five-storey cubes that twist 90° from base to top. Source: Calatrava project page; CTBUH.

q: Which tower was the first great modern tower of iron structure?
n: The Eiffel Tower (1889) was the first great modern tower of iron structure. Source: Société d'Exploitation de la Tour Eiffel; Encyclopaedia Britannica.

q: Which is the only skyscraper Frank Lloyd Wright built?
n: The Price Tower in Bartlesville, Oklahoma (1956) is the only skyscraper Frank Lloyd Wright built. Source: Frank Lloyd Wright Foundation; Price Tower Arts Center.

q: Which style emerged in the early 20th century?
n: Modernism emerged in the early 20th century and spread after World War I. Source: Frampton, Modern Architecture: A Critical History.

q: The only residential project of Ludwig Mies van der Rohe.
n: The Farnsworth House (1951) is the best known of Mies van der Rohe's few houses and the one usually cited as his residential masterwork. Source: Farnsworth House (National Trust) official site.

q: Who designed the TWA Flight Center in New York?
n: The TWA Flight Center at JFK (1962) was designed by Eero Saarinen. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Eero Saarinen.

q: Known for his futuristic and modern designs.
n: Santiago Calatrava is known for futuristic, skeletal, organic designs such as the City of Arts and Sciences in Valencia. Source: Santiago Calatrava official site.

q: What was the world's tallest building as of 2022?
n: As of 2022, the Burj Khalifa (828 m) was the world's tallest building, with Merdeka 118 second once completed. Source: CTBUH Skyscraper Center.

q: Who is called the father of modern architecture in Austria, his work expressing functionalism?
n: Otto Wagner is called the father of modern architecture in Austria. His Vienna Postal Savings Bank expresses functionalism. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Otto Wagner.

q: Who is called the father of modern architecture in Germany?
n: Peter Behrens is called the father of modern architecture in Germany. Gropius, Mies and Le Corbusier worked in his office. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Peter Behrens.

q: Who is called the father of modern architecture in France?
n: Auguste Perret is called the father of modern architecture in France, a pioneer of reinforced concrete. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Auguste Perret.

q: Who is called the father of modern architecture in Holland?
n: Hendrik Berlage is called the father of modern architecture in Holland. His work includes the Amsterdam Stock Exchange (Beurs). Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Hendrik Petrus Berlage.

q: Who pioneered reinforced concrete and designed Notre-Dame du Raincy?
n: Auguste Perret pioneered reinforced concrete architecture. His Notre-Dame du Raincy (1923) is an all-concrete church. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Auguste Perret.

q: Which radical 1920s house in the Netherlands is a De Stijl landmark?
n: The Rietveld Schröder House in Utrecht (1924) is a De Stijl landmark. Source: UNESCO (Rietveld Schröderhuis).

q: In what style is the Schröder House?
n: The Schröder House is in the De Stijl style: intersecting planes and primary colors. Source: UNESCO (Rietveld Schröderhuis).

q: Who designed the Schröder House?
n: Gerrit Rietveld designed the Schröder House. He is also known for the Red Blue Chair. Source: UNESCO (Rietveld Schröderhuis); Centraal Museum Utrecht.

q: Which colors does De Stijl use, as in the Schröder House?
o: Primary colors with black, white and gray
n: De Stijl uses the primary colors red, yellow and blue with black, white and gray. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, De Stijl.

q: What defines the Schröder House's upper floor plan?
o: Open, flexible space with sliding and rotating partitions
n: The upper floor of the Schröder House is open and flexible, divided by sliding and rotating partitions into rooms or one open space. Source: UNESCO (Rietveld Schröderhuis); Centraal Museum Utrecht.

q: What was Taipei 101's former name?
n: Taipei 101 was originally named the Taipei World Financial Center. It was renamed for its 101 floors. Source: Taipei 101 official site.

q: Who designed Taipei 101?
n: Taipei 101 (2004) was designed by C.Y. Lee & Partners. At 508 m it was the world's tallest building until 2010. Its form draws on pagodas and bamboo. Source: Taipei 101 official site; CTBUH.

q: Which building surpassed Taipei 101 as the world's tallest?
n: The Burj Khalifa (828 m) surpassed Taipei 101 as the world's tallest building when it opened in 2010. Source: CTBUH Skyscraper Center.

q: What natural form inspired Taipei 101?
n: Taipei 101's form is inspired by bamboo: eight stacked, flared segments evoke its growth and the Chinese lucky number eight. Source: Taipei 101 official site.

q: What was added to Taipei 101 to resist earthquakes and typhoons?
n: Taipei 101 has a 660-tonne steel tuned mass damper suspended near the top that counteracts sway from typhoons and earthquakes. Source: Taipei 101 official site; CTBUH.

q: Who was the lead architect of the Burj Al Arab project?
n: Tom Wright led the design of the Burj Al Arab while at WS Atkins, and later founded WKK Architects. Source: WKK Architects; Jumeirah Burj Al Arab history.

q: What is the name of Dubai's grandiose structure themed around the mythical lost city, incorporating the flavor of Arabia?
n: Atlantis The Palm in Dubai is themed on the mythical lost city of Atlantis with Arabian flavor. Source: Atlantis The Palm official site.

q: Which firm designed Atlantis The Palm in Dubai?
n: Atlantis The Palm was designed by WATG (Wimberly, Allison, Tong & Goo). The resort's Royal Towers are linked by a giant arched bridge suite at the head of the Palm Jumeirah. Source: WATG project page.

q: Where is Century Spire?
n: Century Spire is in Century City, Makati, Metro Manila. The tower was designed by Daniel Libeskind for Century Properties, and its interiors are by Armani/Casa. Source: Century Properties official site.

q: Who was the conceptual architect of Century Spire?
n: Daniel Libeskind was the conceptual architect of Century Spire, with interiors by Giorgio Armani's team. Source: Studio Libeskind project page; Century Properties.

q: Which Copenhagen housing project stacks apartments over parking to make an artificial hillside?
n: The Mountain Dwellings in Ørestad, Copenhagen (2008) stack terraced apartments over a parking structure, forming an artificial hillside. Source: BIG (Bjarke Ingels Group) project page.

q: Which Danish architect designed the Mountain Dwellings?
n: Bjarke Ingels (BIG, with JDS in the early phase) designed the Mountain Dwellings. Source: BIG project page.
